claim: Storing a failure with a causal explanation, indexed by the goal features that jointly caused it, lets a planner warn itself before planning (CHEF beef-and-broccoli: 3 index features, 20 TOPs, 3 repair strategies). This is a design result with no quantitative test.
agent_test: Lesson entries with trigger features + cause + repair vs plain 'what went wrong' notes, equal tokens, on held-out repeated trap families.

claim: Failure-indexed reminding (Riesbeck ALFRED, Schank and Leake SWALE) rests on anomaly detection: a rule is questioned only when a later case contradicts it. Explanations produced by remindings can be fanciful and need filtering (SWALE: 3 remindings gave 6 explanations, some ruled out).
agent_test: Count how often a retrieved lesson fires on non-matching tasks; require a relevance check before use.

claim: Verbal reflection on a failed trial raises success over repeated attempts when there is a trustworthy outcome signal: Reflexion ALFWorld 130/134 solved in 12 trials (+22 points), HotPotQA +20, HumanEval pass@1 91 vs 80 (GPT-4). Gap search: a bare wrong-flag retry recovers about half the gain on previously wrong items (GPT-4 0.786 to 0.827, vs 0.925 with solution reflection).
agent_test: Reflect-and-retry vs plain retry (best-of-N) at equal tokens, with an oracle outcome and with a self-judged outcome.

claim: Natural-language reflection adds value beyond bare episodic memory and beyond bare test feedback: +8 points on HotPotQA over episodic memory only; HumanEval-Rust (50 hardest, GPT-4) 0.60 base, 0.52 reflection without test generation, 0.60 tests without reflection, 0.68 both.
agent_test: Ablate reflection text vs raw failure trace in memory at equal tokens.

claim: Reflection fails when the failure signal is weak or wrong: Reflexion WebShop no gain after 4 trials; false-positive test passes (MBPP 16.3% vs HumanEval 1.4%) cap gains; hallucination loop in 22% of ALFWorld runs.
agent_test: Measure the false-positive rate of the self-check; do not store a lesson from an unverified failure.

claim: Mis-diagnosed failure memories are harmful: in frozen-environment logs 0 of 121 reflections named the true blocking object; frozen envs took 7.6 trials vs 1.5 (r=0.808 with repeated-reflection ratio); forcing the reflection to quote a trace step raised object mention from 0% to 86%.
agent_test: Require each lesson to quote the trace step that supports it; compare with free-form lessons.

claim: Distilled insights from successes and failures do not uniformly beat raw-case retrieval: ExpeL insights-only vs retrieve-only HotpotQA 36 vs 31, ALFWorld 50 vs 55, WebShop 37 vs 38. ExpeL one attempt on ALFWorld 59.0 vs ReAct+Reflexion R3 54.4 (a19 and c04 had the order reversed).
agent_test: Insights vs raw cases vs both at equal tokens, per task type.

claim: Retrieval quality and memory size control the value of stored cases: ExpeL ALFWorld task-similarity retrieval 59.0 vs reason-similarity 48.5 vs random 42.5 vs ReAct 40.0; Memento best at K=4 with larger K flat or worse; strict-evaluator or capped memory beat add-all.
agent_test: Sweep retrieved-lesson count K and selector type at equal context tokens.
audit_note: ExpeL ablation table columns are garbled in extraction but values 40.0/48.5/42.5/59.0 are consistent; Memento K=4 best is on DeepResearcher average F1 (64.5 vs 63.9-64.1 for larger K).

claim: Adding failure traces helps only if the memory design distils them: ReasoningBank WebArena-Shopping (Gemini-2.5-flash) 46.5 success-only to 49.7 with failures; Synapse 40.6 to 41.7; AWM 44.4 to 42.2 (worse). Overall WebArena +8.3/+7.2/+4.6 over no memory across three backbones.
agent_test: Add failures to a lesson store with and without abstraction into strategy-level lessons.

claim: Failure-derived memory tolerates moderate judge noise but the real judge was only 72.7% accurate: success flat across 70-90% simulated judge accuracy, about 50.6 at the top vs 47.6 at 50% (Shopping subset only). Gap search: MemGuard verifier agreed 86% with inspection and had 88.1% balanced accuracy against benchmark outcomes; 30% simulated label noise degraded but did not erase gains. Break-even accuracy still unmeasured.
agent_test: Run the outcome judge at 70-80% accuracy and check lesson-store degradation.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without an external signal does not help and can hurt: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 (3 calls) and 41.8 (5 calls); GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; with oracle labels GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, GPT-4 HotpotQA 49 to 59 (c12 oracle numbers are wrong, see critique). Gap search: Kamoi survey (mid-2024) found no fair-setting success; for reasoning models extra self-correction gives only marginal gains (CorrectBench) and the blind spot is small or negative (Tsui).
agent_test: Self-revise with and without an external check at equal tokens; accept a revision only if the check passes.
audit_note: Table 1 of Huang et al. checked; gap-search statements match Kamoi, CorrectBench, Tsui.

claim: Models fail mainly at locating their own errors, not fixing them: GPT-4 finds the first error in only 52.87% of 2186 BIG-Bench Mistake traces; given the location, backtracking fixes 23.53% of wrong word-sorting traces (and breaks 11.11% of correct ones); 14 open models show a 64.5% blind spot to own errors vs identical external errors.
agent_test: Critic given the error step vs critic that must find it, equal tokens.
audit_note: Tsui's 14 models are open non-reasoning models (reasoning models show a small or negative blind spot); the 23.53%/11.11% figures use an oracle mistake location and PaLM 2 traces.

claim: Quality of the error explanation bounds repair: GPT-4 repairing with its own feedback 33.30% vs with human feedback 52.60% on APPS (competition level 3.67% vs 14.67%).
agent_test: Swap a self-written lesson for a stronger-model or human-written one and measure the repair gap.

claim: Negative examples help training only when high quality: +8.74 with high-quality vs -3.16 with low-quality negatives (7B, 2k positives); gain shrinks to +0.52 at 13B with 5k positives. LEMA correction data gives +0.3 to +4.6 across five models and did not beat equal-size CoT data for LLaMA-2-7B.
agent_test: Filter stored lessons by verified quality; compare filtered vs unfiltered at equal tokens.

claim: Structured step-level failure attribution lets an agent recover: AgentDebug all-correct 24.3% vs 0.3% best baseline, step accuracy 45.0 vs 28.0; ALFWorld success up to +26% relative.
agent_test: Diagnose-then-retry with a taxonomy vs free reflection at equal tokens.

claim: Clustering failures in batches into short guidance can beat big memories on tokens: Mistake Notebook Learning KaggleDBQA 24.0 to 64.0 with 514 guidance tokens vs ACE 54.0 with 9406 tokens (one model); other backbones gained 6-9 points.
agent_test: Compare compact clustered lessons with full-trajectory memory at the same token budget.

claim: Reflection does not help when the failure cause is exploration or missing environment knowledge: Reflexion@5 gave no gain over re-execute@5 on cross-app tasks; a count-based exploration hint gave +27% on the Camera app; hindsight prompts trailed exploration-only by about 4 points on HotpotQA (GPT-3.5). In tension with the positive Reflexion results. Gap search: VRL-Bench (d04) finds each reflection method beats memory-free retry in some settings and loses in others; a model-chosen explore/exploit scheduler was the only positive-over-retry update in all 6 settings. Reflection is a policy with a cost, not a free gain.
agent_test: Classify failures as knowledge, exploration or execution before choosing reflect vs explore.

claim: Memory pollution and drift: online AWM workflows from unverified trajectories can degrade results, and add-all memory with a weak evaluator is flat or declining. Gap search: LLM consolidation itself erodes memory (GPT-5.4 dropped from 100% to 54% accuracy, i.e. failed 46% of a 19-problem ARC-AGI slice it solved without memory), and history-based deletion with a reliable evaluator helps.
agent_test: Gate memory writes on verified success; compare with add-all.
audit_note: Zhang et al.'s abstract says GPT-5.4 'fails on 54%' but the body (intro and results) says accuracy fell from 100% to 54% on a 19-problem slice, i.e. it failed on 46%; the claim repeats the abstract's misstatement.
claim_before_audit: Memory pollution and drift: online AWM workflows from unverified trajectories can degrade results, and add-all memory with a weak evaluator is flat or declining. Gap search: LLM consolidation itself erodes memory (GPT-5.4 failed 54% of ARC-AGI problems it solved without memory), and history-based deletion with a reliable evaluator helps.

claim: More feedback per stored LLM case is not monotone: double-feedback cases beat single in 3 trials and lost in 6 (not significant).
agent_test: Replicate on our own lesson store.

claim: Retroformer reports gains over Reflexion-type baselines (HotPotQA +18%, AlfWorld +36%, WebShop +4%) by training the reflection writer, so learned lesson writing may beat prompted lesson writing.
agent_test: Not testable without training; note only.

claim: At equal token cost, reflect-and-retry does not beat plain resampling on small models: Self-Refine and forced Reflexion stay 3.6 to 10.1 points below self-consistency at 7B; 0 of 36 method-setting comparisons beat it, 10 are worse; code self-repair loses 6.1 points to blind resampling at 1.5B and ties at 7B with 2.5x to 5.5x more tokens. Untested at frontier scale and with external test signals.
agent_test: Always include an equal-token resample arm; log whether self-triggered retries ever fire.

claim: Showing a model its own failed attempt anchors it: near-identical retry in 33-68% of retries vs 2-14% for blind resampling; execution feedback adds nothing beyond a content-free wrong notice; retrieved solutions to other tasks change nothing (within 3.5 points).
agent_test: Compare lessons that restate the trap and alternative against lessons that replay the failed output; log consecutive-attempt similarity.

claim: Richer failure reflections beat thin ones when a wrong-flag is given: GPT-4 on previously wrong items baseline 0.786, retry 0.827, advice 0.840, explanation 0.876, solution 0.925 (nine models, all p<0.001). Some of the gain is the oracle signal itself and some is answer leakage.
agent_test: Explanation-plus-repair lesson vs bare retry vs bare what-went-wrong, equal tokens, no oracle flag.

claim: A separate failure-guard channel adds about 1 to 2 points; governance (dedupe, staleness, conflict, admission) adds 4 to 7: MemGuard Qwen-3.5-Plus without failure memories 66.1/82.2/56.5/50.7 vs full 67.4/83.6/58.4/51.8; without governance 63.7/79.8/52.0/46.8. Failure-only memory beat success-only by 0.8 points (U-Mem, within noise); hybrid best. No isolated warning-vs-recipe test exists.
agent_test: Cap warnings at 2, label with trigger; count false firings on non-matching tasks using p > (G+c)/(L+G).

claim: Retrieve a small number of lessons: U-Mem K=1 50.20, K=3 52.40, K=5 50.80, K=10 48.80 (HotpotQA, 7B). Raw episodes held up better than LLM-consolidated lessons, which first help then fall below no-memory (Zhang et al.). Granularity and K have not been swept together.
agent_test: 2x3 sweep: raw vs insight vs cluster, K in {2,4,8}.

claim: Use-history deletion helps only with a reliable utility evaluator and can hurt with a weak one (Xiong: GPT-4o-mini evaluator helped one agent, hurt another); an append-only store loses 3.2 points to merge/delete (U-Mem). Best supported rule: periodic plus history-based deletion.
agent_test: Equal-size stores under FIFO, periodic, history-based and combined deletion.

claim: Forced re-check triggers: appending Wait cuts the self-correction blind spot by 89.3% on non-reasoning models (DeepSeek-V3 0.567 to 0.902, R1-0528 0.908), but reasoning models already show a small or negative blind spot and extra correction loops add only marginal gains.
agent_test: Wait-trigger arm vs none on a non-reasoning base, and on a reasoning base.

claim: No independent modern replication of CHEF-style failure-indexed retrieval was found in ICCBR 2025 or the LLM-agent literature; nearest analogues are signed negative cards (ConMem) and failure guards (MemGuard), both ablated only as bundled components.
agent_test: Direct CHEF-style arm (trigger features + cause + repair) vs plain reflection, held-out trap families.
